headline: The AI unwind jumped from chips to the metals pits — copper -4.1%, platinum -4.2%, gold to a 52-week low — while the dollar printed a new high and NVDA's blowout quarter bought nothing.
summary: What changed today is the location of the pain. For three weeks this was a de-rating of semis and power names; today it was a liquidation of hard assets. Copper -4.1% to 5.729 (z=-1.98, -12.4% on the month), platinum -4.2%, silver -3.1%, gold -2.0% to 3,788.8 and sitting at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range. Brent -3.5%, WTI -2.5% and now -19.1% on the month; DBC's one-month move is z=-2.27. Bloomberg's tape attributed the Asian-session rout to AI-linked metals (tin -8.2% intraday), which matters because Nvidia delivered Q3 revenue of $115.8bn, +103% y/y, after Tuesday's close — and the market answered by selling the physical inputs. The digest's last NVDA mark is 155.46, -27.4% in a month, 0th percentile, 23.6% below its 200-day.

The transmission mechanism is still the dollar and the real rate. DXY 103.79, +0.3% and at the 100th percentile; EURUSD 1.0971 at the 0th; USDCHF 0.8426 at the 100th with acceleration z=0.78. USDBRL 5.7968 is the most violent print on the board — +14.5% in a month, z=4.08, acceleration 3.04 — and explains why EWZ is -25.8% on the month against Bovespa -17.2%. Meanwhile the 10-year real yield is 2.92%, +26bp on the week and 29% above its 200-day, against a 10-year breakeven of 2.21% at the 9th percentile and a 5-year at 2.26%. Commodities crashing into a 9th-percentile breakeven is a deflationary impulse the nominal curve has not yet discounted: 10s only fell 3bp to 5.12%. The inflation composite still reads +35 because core CPI (z=0.93) is turning up — that is October's data arguing with today's prices.

The offsets are intact and got cheaper. VIX fell 6.5% to 23.80 and CCCs tightened 6bp after +292bp in three months; HY OAS is still only +3bp on the month and BKLN sits at the 94th percentile. Breadth still refuses to break: equal-weight/cap-weight z=2.46 with acceleration 1.69, transports/S&P z=2.12, small caps/S&P acceleration 1.95. The energy-price rebate is showing up in cash flows — gasoline -22.6% on the month, UPS +14.8% (z=1.87), FDX +9.0%, MCD +13.5% (z=2.52), COST +12.4%, HD +9.5% — and mortgages at 7.11%, -29bp with acceleration z=-2.36, have ITB +6.2%. Labour is not the problem: claims 200k, continuing claims 1.697m at the 1st percentile, JOLTS 7,523 and +4.6%.

Two things deteriorated versus yesterday. First, the hiding place broke: software, which had outperformed semis by 7.7% on the month, gave back 2.9% in a single session — IGV -3.3%, ORCL -3.4%, MSFT -2.3%, PLTR -2.4% — while semis actually stabilised (SOXX +0.2%, AVGO +2.5%, KOSPI +2.0%, TAIEX +0.3%). Second, the vol curve is still inverted at 1.0192 (76th percentile) with VIX3M +21.9% on the month and SKEW at z=-2.10: the whole curve has repriced higher and nobody owns tails. Crypto remains the cleanest read on leverage — BTC -13.6% on the week and -22% on the month, SOL -29.2%, MSTR -29.5%, COIN at the 0th percentile. Risk regime -19 from -17; rates composite -53, dollar -48.

good.text: The energy and food collapse is a consumer rebate that is already in earnings: gasoline -22.6% and WTI -19.1% on the month feeding UPS +14.8% (z=1.87, acc 1.34), FDX +9.0%, MCD +13.5% (z=2.52), COST +12.4%, HD +9.5%, with retail/S&P at z=1.19.

Breadth is still the bull case: equal-weight/cap-weight z=2.46 with acceleration 1.69, RSP +0.8% on the month against SPX -4.2%, transports/S&P z=2.12, small caps/S&P acceleration 1.95. This is one crowded trade unwinding, not a broad growth scare.

Credit did not follow through on yesterday's 11bp HY gap: CCC spreads tightened 6bp (acc z=-2.17), HY is flat on the week and only +3bp on the month, BKLN sits at the 94th percentile and HYG/IEF is turning up with acceleration 0.59.

The front end is leaning toward relief: 2s -5bp to 4.83%, 5s -5bp, 10s -3bp, and mortgages at 7.11%, -29bp on the month with acceleration z=-2.36 — housing equities responded, ITB +6.2% and XHB +4.4% on the month, starts +9.9%.

Asia found a bid while the West sold metals: KOSPI +2.0%, TAIEX +0.3%, Nikkei +0.3%, and India keeps breaking out — Sensex +11.1% on the month (z=2.61, acc 2.04), INDA z=1.98, rupee firmer with USDINR -1.6% on the month.

Labour and the defensive cash-flow complex are unbothered: claims 200k, continuing claims 1.697m at the 1st percentile, JOLTS +4.6%; XLV outperforming by 9.2% on the month with LLY +12.7% and medical devices z=1.09.

bad.text: The AI unwind reached physical commodities: copper -4.1% (z=-1.98), platinum -4.2%, silver -3.1%, gold -2.0% at the 0th percentile of 52 weeks. Copper miners -18.3% on the month, XME at the 4th percentile, FCX -20.5%, and copper/gold rolled -2.2% — the growth signal, not just a positioning flush.

The dollar is the accelerant and it is still accelerating in the wrong places: DXY 103.79 at the 100th percentile, EURUSD at the 0th, USDCHF at the 100th with acceleration 0.78, and USDBRL +14.5% on the month at z=4.08 with acceleration 3.04 — the fastest tightening on the board.

A real-rate squeeze into a disinflation shock: 10-year real yield 2.92%, +26bp on the week and 29% above its 200-day, against 10-year breakevens of 2.21% at the 9th percentile. MOVE is +35.9% in three months. Nominal 10s at 5.12% have not discounted the commodity bust.

The rotation hiding place cracked: software/semis gave back 2.9% in one session after +7.7% on the month, IGV -3.3%, ORCL -3.4%, MSFT -2.3%, PLTR -2.4%. When the defensive leg of a crowded unwind starts selling, it is de-grossing, not rotation.

Tails are unowned into an inverted curve: VIX/VIX3M 1.0192 at the 76th percentile, VIX3M +21.9% on the month, SKEW 145.1 at z=-2.10. Today's VIX drop to 23.80 lowers the cost of protection without fixing the structure.

Leverage is still being liquidated in crypto: BTC -13.6% on the week and -22% on the month, ETH -25.5%, SOL -29.2%, MSTR -6.3% today and -29.5% on the month, COIN at the 0th percentile — with bank reserves -2.3% and net liquidity -0.4% on the month.

trades.name: Duration against the commodity bust
trades.line: Long TLT: commodity crash vs 9th-percentile breakevens
trades.expr: Buy TLT outright (79.55); add Jan 85 calls for convexity. Futures equivalent: long 10y/30y Treasury futures.
trades.thesis: Commodities are telling you the inflation impulse is over — DBC one-month move z=-2.27, WTI -19.1%, gasoline -22.6%, copper -12.4% — while nominal 10s have only fallen 3bp to 5.12% and the real yield sits 29% above its 200-day. Breakevens at the 9th percentile plus a 100th-percentile dollar is an import-price shock on top. Something has to give, and it is the nominal yield.
trades.trigger: Copper -4.1%, Brent -3.5% and gold -2.0% in one session; 10-year breakeven 2.21%, 5-year 2.26%; 2s and 5s already down 5bp while TLT sits at the 25th percentile of its 52-week range.
trades.stop: 10-year back above 5.30% / TLT below 76.5, or breakevens turning back up with core CPI accelerating further (core CPI already z=0.93, turning up).

trades.name: Brazil: currency, not equity
trades.line: Long USDBRL vs short EWZ: the squeeze is still accelerating
trades.expr: Long USD/BRL spot or 1-month forward, half-sized short in EWZ against it. Cap the FX leg — carry is against you.
trades.thesis: USDBRL at z=4.08 with acceleration 3.04 is the single most extreme reading in the digest, and the gap between Bovespa -17.2% and EWZ -25.8% on the month is pure currency. With copper, crude and iron-ore proxies all liquidating, Brazil's terms of trade are deteriorating into the squeeze. EM FX has no stabiliser while DXY is at the 100th percentile.
trades.trigger: USDBRL +0.2% today to 5.7968 after +3.8% on the week; EWZ one-month move z=-3.33 with acceleration -3.15; broad EM currency basket rolling over (CEW -1.2% on the month).
trades.stop: USDBRL back below 5.55, or DXY breaking below its 200-day (currently 3.9% above).

trades.name: Energy equity hasn't paid for the crude crash
trades.line: Short XLE vs long XRT: crude -18%, XLE still 7% over 200d
trades.expr: Short XLE (or XOP for more beta), long XRT dollar-for-dollar.
trades.thesis: Brent is -18.0% on the month and -3.5% today, yet XLE is still 7.3% above its 200-day at the 76th percentile with three-month relative strength of +4.6%. That lag closes. The same barrel that de-rates energy earnings is a direct transfer to the consumer: gasoline -22.6% on the month, retail/S&P z=1.19 and turning up.
trades.trigger: Today's session: Brent -3.5%, WTI -2.5%, gasoline -2.5%; XOP -11.4% and OIH -7.3% on the month have begun to converge to the commodity while the cap-weighted sector has not.
trades.stop: Brent back above 98 (supply event), or XRT losing its 200-day (currently +3.3%).

trades.name: Own protection while it is cheap again
trades.line: Short SPHB vs long SPLV: inverted VIX curve, zero tail demand
trades.expr: Short SPHB against long SPLV; overlay with December SPY 5% OTM puts funded by selling 10% OTM — SKEW at z=-2.10 makes the wing cheap relative to the body.
trades.thesis: The vol curve is inverted (VIX/VIX3M 1.0192, 76th percentile) with VIX3M +21.9% on the month, yet SKEW is at z=-2.10 — the market has repriced the body of the distribution and abandoned the tail. High-beta/low-vol is -12.1% on the month (z=-1.92) and momentum is -10.9% (z=-2.03); that trend persists while de-grossing runs.
trades.trigger: VIX fell 6.5% to 23.80 today, cheapening the hedge, while the term structure stayed inverted and software — the last rotation refuge — broke (IGV -3.3%).
trades.stop: VIX/VIX3M back below 0.92 with SPX reclaiming 7,600; SPHB/SPLV recovering its 200-day (now 11.8% above spot).
trades.target: 6-8% on the pair; SPX 7,000 on the option leg.

trades.name: India is the only EM with a bid
trades.line: Long INDA vs short EEM: oil importer, strengthening rupee
trades.thesis: India is the inverse of the commodity-exporter squeeze: crude -19.1% on the month is a terms-of-trade windfall, and the rupee is the only EM currency strengthening (USDINR -1.6% on the month, z=-1.71, -0.6% today). Sensex is +11.1% on the month at z=2.61 with acceleration 2.04 — the strongest trend reading in global equities — against EEM -7.3% and EEM/SPY at the 6th percentile.
trades.trigger: Sensex and INDA both extended again while Korea, Taiwan and Brazil carried the EM index lower; INDA +0.7% with one-month relative strength of +13.5%.
trades.stop: USDINR back above 95, or Brent reclaiming 100; INDA/EEM giving back half the one-month gain.

trades.name: Crypto leverage is still unwinding
trades.line: Short MSTR: BTC -22% on the month, premium compression
trades.expr: Short MSTR outright, or buy January puts; size small — this is a high-vol short.
trades.thesis: Bitcoin at 63,884 is -13.6% on the week, -22% on the month and 11.4% below its 200-day at the 14th percentile. Levered equity proxies decay faster than the asset: MSTR -6.3% today versus BTC -1.6%, -29.5% on the month, COIN -33.6% and at the 0th percentile. With bank reserves -2.3% and net liquidity -0.4% on the month, there is no marginal funding bid to stop it.
trades.trigger: Today's divergence — MSTR fell four times bitcoin's move — plus IBIT -21.7% on the month with acceleration z=-1.42 showing ETF outflows, not accumulation.
trades.stop: BTC reclaiming 72,000 / its 200-day; MSTR up 15% from entry.

trades.name: Earnings you can touch versus capex you can't
trades.line: Long XLV vs short XLK: health care trend, tech still rolling
trades.expr: Long XLV, short XLK dollar-for-dollar; express the long leg via LLY/IHI if you want more trend.
trades.thesis: XLV is +4.8% on the month at the 91st percentile and 16.1% above its 200-day, outperforming by 9.2% on the month and 14.5% over three; XLK is -11.0% on the month (z=-1.90), 4.3% below its 200-day and underperforming by 7.3%. Nvidia's $115.8bn quarter couldn't lift the complex — when a 103% growth print doesn't pay, the de-rating is about multiples and funding, not fundamentals.
trades.trigger: UNH -5.4% today gives a better entry on the long leg without breaking the sector trend (XLV still up, 91st percentile), while tech's second line broke today: MSFT -2.3%, ORCL -3.4%, IGV -3.3%.
trades.stop: XLK relative strength turning up / SMH reclaiming its 200-day (12.2% above spot); XLV losing 175.
